lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Remember little browser games from the early 2010s? Most of them died when Flash did.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: FlashGames is Antoine's way of keeping some of his own creations playable. It's a small collection of ActionScript games with their assets included.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But browsers dropped Flash. How do they run?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With Ruffle, a Flash player that runs in the browser. The page picks a game file and hands it to Ruffle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the game and the page are separate.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, the game file and the HTML around it are two distinct pieces, which keeps the whole thing simple. It's a single static page under the MIT license, and there's a play online link.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A little time capsule you can click.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The full page explains the components.
